title: Comparing Two Online Music Programs for Older Adults With Memory Difficulties
official: Impact of Two Different Virtual Online Groups for Older Adults With Mild Cognitive Decline
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an online group singing intervention for older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is it feasible to deliver an online group singing intervention to older adults with MCI?
* Is the online group singing intervention acceptable and satisfactory to participants?

Researchers will compare online group singing with online music history education to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of the two programs and explore their effects on cognitive, emotional, and psychosocial outcomes.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to participate in either online group singing or online music history education.
* Attend regularly scheduled online group sessions.
* Complete questionnaires and assessments of cognitive function, emotional well-being, and psychosocial outcomes at designated study time points.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or subjective memory decline (SMD) with objectively low Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores (between 17 and 25).
* English language fluency rated as fairly well or better.
* Not currently participating in a choir or chorus.
* Access to a wireless internet connection at home or wherever the participant plans to participate in the virtual groups.
* Access to a desktop or laptop computer with the capability to connect to an internet router via an Ethernet cable.
* Not currently taking psychoactive medications or sleep medications that could adversely affect cognitive abilities.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Medical diagnosis of dementia (of any etiology)
* Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score \< 17
* Current (but not prior) severe psychiatric disorder
* Serious medical condition (e.g., stroke or transient ischemic attack) that would interfere with study participation.
* Poor English language fluency.
* Currently participating in a choir or chorus
* Plans to travel for more than one week during the intervention period to a location without internet access (where the participant cannot access the online program).
* Plans to move out of the area within 6 months (Phase 2 only)
* Limited life expectancy (e.g., enrollment in hospice or metastatic cancer) (Phase 2 only)
* Initiation of dementia medication (cholinesterase inhibitor or memantine within past three months or plans to initiate dementia medication during the study period (Phase 2 only).
* Plans to initiate or change psychoactive medication during the study period (Phase 2 only).
